status_summary: The Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28), enacted 2025-07-24, rescinded CPB's FY2026 and FY2027 advance appropriations, about $1.07 billion per CRS. CPB announced a wind-down in 2025, filed to dissolve in January 2026, and pending CPB board litigation was dismissed as moot. Separately, on 2026-03-31 Judge Randolph Moss ruled that Executive Order 14290, which aimed to end federal funding for NPR and PBS, violates the First Amendment and permanently enjoined its implementation; he found the CPB claims moot because CPB had dissolved, so the ruling does not restore CPB funding. No CPB appropriation was enacted for FY2026, per Current, and the FY2027 stopgap (Public Law 119-103, enacted 2026-09-02, through 2026-12-11) continues FY2026 rates and contains no CPB provision. As of April 2026 some lawmakers sought money for tribal and rural stations through other accounts.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14290, directing the CPB board and federal agencies to end direct and indirect funding for NPR and PBS to the extent the law allows.
House passes the rescission bill (H.R. 4), 214-212, including CPB's advance appropriations.

Senate passes the amended rescission bill 51-48; the enacted act included all appropriations covered by the President's special message, which had requested rescission of about $1.07 billion in CPB funds for FY2026 and FY2027.

The Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28) is enacted; section 2(b)(20) rescinds the amounts made available to CPB for FY2026 (Public Law 118-47) and FY2027 (Public Law 119-4), about $1.07 billion per CRS.

CPB announces an orderly wind-down of its operations after the rescission package and a Senate FY2026 Labor-HHS bill that omits CPB funding, with most staff positions ending on 2025-09-30 and a small transition team remaining through January 2026.

A Congressional Research Service report states that Public Law 119-28 rescinded CPB's FY2026 and FY2027 advance appropriations, that the White House FY2026 budget had proposed cancelling them, and that Senate appropriators excluded CPB from the FY2026 Labor-HHS bill.
CPB announces it is filing to dissolve; on 2026-01-14 Judge Moss dismisses two pending CPB lawsuits as moot.

Judge Moss (D.D.C.), in NPR v. Trump (No. 1:25-cv-01674), rules that Executive Order 14290 violates the First Amendment and permanently enjoins agency defendants from implementing it; the claims concerning CPB are moot because CPB has dissolved, and the court directs a joint status report on next steps, including whether to enter partial final judgment.

The Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (Public Law 119-103) is enacted, funding agencies through 2026-12-11 at FY2026 rates and barring new starts; its text contains no provision for CPB or public broadcasting.

title: End federal funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting
uncertainties: A case tracker (Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse) lists a partial final judgment on 2026-04-23, but it could not be confirmed in a court record or news, and no notice of appeal was found in the tracker, the GovInfo court package or news searches; CourtListener and congress.gov were not reachable from this review. The CPB wind-down announcement of 2025-08-01 is confirmed in CPB's own news release. The absence of FY2027 CPB funding rests on the stopgap text and a CRS overview; full-year FY2027 bills had not been enacted as of 2026-10-12, and the search tools returned limited recent coverage. CPB's authorizing statute has not been repealed, so a future Congress could fund public broadcasting again.
